title: 1 Corinthians
tagline: Paul answers a divided, gifted, and troubled church in a bustling Greek port city.
author: Paul
authorNote: The letter names Paul as author (1:1, 16:21), and nearly all scholars accept that. Sosthenes is named with him as a co-sender (1:1); Paul probably dictated and then added a greeting in his own hand (16:21). Some scholars think a few verses (such as 14:34-35) may have been added later, and a few debate whether our letter combines more than one of Paul's letters to Corinth. Paul mentions an earlier letter that we do not have (5:9).
audience: The church in Corinth, a mixed group of mostly Gentile believers, many of them poor, with a few of higher status
audienceNote: Paul founded the church on his second journey and stayed about eighteen months (Acts 18). Corinth was a Roman colony and a wealthy port with two harbors, known for trade, religious variety, and a reputation for loose living. The church wrote to Paul with questions (7:1) and Chloe's people reported quarrels (1:11).
setting: Ephesus, about AD 54 to 55, a few years after Paul's time in Corinth
settingNote: Paul writes from Ephesus (16:8), during his third journey, planning to pass through Macedonia and come to Corinth (16:5-8). The date comes from the timeline of Acts and from Gallio's governorship in Achaia (Acts 18:12), and is good but not certain. The letter was probably carried by Stephanas, Fortunatus, and Achaicus (16:17).
genreNote: A pastoral letter that answers reports and written questions one by one. Paul often moves from a problem to a principle and back to a practical answer, and sometimes quotes slogans from the Corinthians (such as "all things are lawful for me") before correcting them.
bigIdea: The cross reshapes everything. Because Christ was crucified and raised, a divided and proud church is called to be one body, shaped by love, and to look forward to resurrection.
mapTitle: Map: Corinth, Ephesus, Macedonia, and Jerusalem
mapSummary: Paul writes from Ephesus to Corinth across the Aegean Sea, plans a route through Macedonia, and is gathering money for the poor in Jerusalem.
